authorization_instruction: continue from here to as far as you can. dont stop for reports. you know i trust in your recommendations. complete the bootstraps if possible. but if you absolutely require my input for something thats a design choice that hasnt been decided yet, then defer it and build around it - if possible.

authoring.title: The certified registry and oracle preserve semantic body orientation
authoring.claim: In the exact certified BR12.0 fixtures, the strict registry preserves declared semantic body-region contact roles, distinguishes steady stance from temporary recovery support, rejects duplicate identities, invalid support policy, and guidance authority, while the labeled-box oracle fixes the authored +X right, +Y up, -Z forward basis, preserves orthonormal handedness, and fails closed on invalid or nonfinite evidence.
authoring.scope: Only the exact body-region role registry, support policy, labeled-box basis convention, validation tolerances, engine, source, and BR12.0 program scope certified by br12_20260723T211754Z_0ace3791.
authoring.mechanism: A sealed semantic registry describes how observed body regions may be interpreted as support. A separate pure basis oracle maps authored labeled-box axes into a validated right-handed orientation without applying mechanics.
applicability: Checking the exact labeled-box right, up, and forward basis before pose classification
failure_boundaries: Role and basis interpretation is observation metadata and does not create or retain physical contact
Temporary ventral recovery support is not steady stance
No controller, dynamic recovery, getting up, free 3D standing or bracing, gait, walking, repair, or guidance is established
unknowns: How labeled regions and support policies should be authored for arbitrary creature morphology
Which basis tolerances remain suitable for noisier runtime observations

authoring.title: The certified classifier preserves canonical pose ambiguity
authoring.claim: In the exact certified BR12.1 fixtures, the deterministic profile-specific classifier combines declared labeled-box orientation and required semantic support contact to classify only upright, prone, supine, left-side, and right-side canonical poses, and returns unknown for ambiguous, conflicting, incomplete, invalid, or nonfinite evidence without granting actuation, repair, or guidance authority.
authoring.scope: Only the exact canonical pose set, labeled-box bases, orientation thresholds, semantic support-contact requirements, unknown behavior, engine, source, and BR12.1 program scope certified by br12_20260723T211754Z_0ace3791.
authoring.mechanism: The pure classifier scores only preregistered pose profiles against validated orientation and contact evidence. It emits a pose label or unknown and has no mechanics output.
applicability: Classifying the five exact certified labeled-box canonical poses
Preserving unknown when canonical-pose evidence conflicts or is insufficient
failure_boundaries: Unknown must not be guessed into the nearest canonical pose
A classified fallen pose is not evidence that a recovery can execute
No controller, physical self-righting, getting up, free 3D recovery, gait, walking, repair, or guidance is established
unknowns: Which pose profiles and thresholds transfer to non-box creature morphologies
How runtime sensor noise should be filtered without erasing genuine ambiguity

authoring.title: The certified recovery profile addresses anatomy by semantic role
authoring.claim: In the exact certified BR12.2 fixtures, the strict recovery profile references anatomy through semantic roles rather than limb indices, binds one exact prone static-feasibility sequence, names every missing required role, rejects duplicates and unknown roles, and exposes no controller, command, contact-creation, repair, or guidance channel.
authoring.scope: Only the exact prone recovery-profile identifier, semantic role vocabulary, required-role set, phase descriptions, missing-role failures, engine, source, and BR12.2 program scope certified by br12_20260723T211754Z_0ace3791.
authoring.mechanism: A declarative recovery profile binds planning phases to semantic anatomy requirements. Validation either returns the exact role mapping or a named infeasible result before actuation.
applicability: Checking whether the exact prone planning profile has every required semantic anatomy role
Producing named missing-role reasons before static feasibility analysis
failure_boundaries: Semantic role matching does not select actuators or issue commands
A complete role match is not static or dynamic feasibility proof
No physical self-righting, getting up, stance handoff, gait, walking, repair, or guidance is established
unknowns: Which canonical morphology should instantiate the first BR13 physical profile
Which alternative profiles are needed for supine and side poses

authoring.title: The certified analyzer rejects statically infeasible recovery phases
authoring.claim: In the exact certified BR12.3 fixtures, the digest-bound analyzer evaluates conservative static torque, power, structural, friction, and reach margins for one exact semantic-role recovery profile, names underpowered, overloaded, slipping, unreachable, and anatomically incomplete phases before actuation, and treats feasible as a planning-screen result rather than dynamic recovery evidence.
authoring.scope: Only the exact recovery profile, anatomy-role mapping, phase loads, conservative margins, torque, power, structural, friction, and reach equations, thresholds, engine, source, and BR12.3 program scope certified by br12_20260723T211754Z_0ace3791.
authoring.mechanism: The pure analyzer evaluates preregistered static inequalities for each declared phase and returns named margins and failure reasons. It emits no command, wrench, joint target, or contact operation.
applicability: Rejecting obviously underpowered, overloaded, slipping, unreachable, or incomplete phases before actuation
Recording exact static feasibility margins for one certified semantic-role recovery profile
failure_boundaries: Static feasibility does not prove dynamic execution, stability, contact transitions, or stance handoff
The analyzer contains no controller, actuation, contact creation, maintenance, or external assistance
